Absci Soars 12%, Schrödinger Up 11%, Recursion Up 9% as AI Drug Discovery Stocks Rally ©Robert Kneschke via Canva
Key Takeaways

Absci rose 12% today, Schrödinger 11% and Recursion 9%, and no company news explains any of the three moves.

Schrödinger's rally has the most business behind it, and Absci's rally is mostly about investors' appetite for risk.

In the second quarter of 2026, Absci had $0.3 million of revenue and burned $27.6 million of free cash flow. Management says its cash lasts into the second half of 2028.

Absci's third-quarter report on Nov. 12 is the next real test.

Absci (ABSI:NASDAQ) shares jumped 12% today. The company's only news was an 8 a.m. note saying it will attend some upcoming investor conferences.

It had plenty of company. Schrödinger (SDGR:NASDAQ) rose 11% and Recursion (RXRX:NASDAQ) gained 9%, while Twist Bioscience, Tempus AI and 10x Genomics rose 8% to 10%. The Nasdaq 100 and the small-cap Russell 2000 each rose 1%, so this looks like a risk-on day lifting the whole group.

Same rally, very different businesses

Schrödinger has real revenue to price: $255.9 million in 2025, up 23% from 2024. And even after a big run off February's lows, its forward price/sales multiple is close to its five-year average.

Schrödinger (SDGR): forward (NTM) price/sales, last 5 years (TIKR)

Today's jump takes it closer to 9x. That's a bit above its average, but nowhere near the nearly 27x it hit in 2021.

Recursion is further from paying its own way. Over the trailing 12 months it had $54.9 million of revenue and a $518.9 million net loss. It did raise $200 million at $3.25 a share on Oct. 15, so the cash is there for now.

TIKR tracks 11 analysts on Absci. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Absci, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Absci's Analyst Ratings

Absci runs on sentiment

Absci is the furthest of the three from its fundamentals. It brought in $0.3 million of revenue in the second quarter of 2026. Even before today's jump, it was worth roughly eight times its cash and short-term investments. That cash rose sharply in the June quarter after a $100 million stock offering, which included a $40 million strategic investment from Eli Lilly…

Absci (ABSI): cash and short-term investments, $ millions, last 8 quarters (to June 30, 2026) (TIKR)

…and Absci has burned $26 million to $29 million of free cash flow in each of the past four quarters:

Absci (ABSI): free cash flow, $ millions, last 8 quarters (to June 30, 2026) (TIKR)

Management says its cash should fund operations into the second half of 2028, so there's no funding crunch coming soon. The valuation rests on ABS-201, which posted positive interim Phase 1 data in the HEADLINE trial this year.

Nov. 12 is the real test

My take: Schrödinger's rally has the most business behind it. Absci's rally is a bet on ABS-201 riding a risk-on day. A stock that jumps 12% on no news can give it back just as fast when the mood turns.

Investing.com - Nasdaq futures advanced on Wednesday after stronger-than-expected results from South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix sparked a global rally in artificial intelligence-linked semiconductor stocks. Investors were also looking ahead to earnings from major technology companies and a Federal Reserve interest rate decision.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

By 06:06 ET (10:06 GMT), Nasdaq 100 futures had gained 132 points, or 0.4%, while S&P 500 futures had risen 10 points, or 0.1%. Dow futures, meanwhile, had dropped 105 points, or 0.2%.

Here are some of the biggest premarket U.S. stock movers today:

SK Hynix shares surged 7.4% in premarket trading to $156.15 after the memory chipmaker reported record third-quarter 2026 results, with revenue exceeding KRW 100 trillion for the first time in a single quarter. Revenue reached KRW 104.62 trillion, while operating profit jumped 632% year-over-year to KRW 83.33 trillion, representing an operating margin of 80% and beating analyst expectations. The company also announced plans to return approximately KRW 100 trillion to shareholders through fiscal 2026, including at least KRW 30 trillion in cash dividends and at least KRW 60 trillion in share repurchases and cancellations, marking its largest shareholder-return commitment to date.

Vertiv Holdings surged 15.1% before the bell after the data-center power and cooling equipment provider reported third-quarter results that comfortably beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year outlook. Adjusted earnings came in at $2.21 per share, above the $1.82 consensus, while revenue jumped 61% year-over-year to $4.31 billion, topping forecasts of $3.75 billion. Organic orders more than doubled from a year earlier, easing concerns that delays in AI-related projects were holding back revenue growth. Vertiv raised its 2026 adjusted earnings forecast to $7.15 per share, compared with the previous consensus of $6.73, and projected revenue of $14.65 billion, above expectations of $13.99 billion. Its fourth-quarter outlook also exceeded analyst estimates.

Ultra Clean Holdings climbed 12% in premarket trading after the semiconductor equipment supplier reported record third-quarter results and issued an upbeat forecast for the current quarter. Adjusted earnings reached $1.15 per share, beating the $0.94 analyst consensus, while revenue rose nearly 49% year-over-year to a record $759 million, above estimates of $728.07 million. Profitability also improved, with non-GAAP gross margin expanding to 17.3% from 15.7% in the previous quarter and operating margin increasing to 9% from 7%. For the fourth quarter, the company forecast revenue of $800 million to $860 million, with the midpoint above the $813.9 million consensus, and adjusted earnings of $1.11 to $1.35 per share.

Google-owner Alphabet and software giant Microsoft are set to headline the slate of post-market earnings -- and potentially shed more light on the AI spending outlook among some of the world's largest companies.

In particular, traders are hunting for any signs of possible returns from Big Tech's planned expenditures -- in some cases ranging into the hundreds of billions of dollars -- on the data centers and chips underpinning AI systems.
